verdict.rationale: Firestore docs state the SDK caches active data so apps can write, read, listen to, and query while the device is offline, and Firebase is positioned to 'store and sync app data.' Together these cover the core offline-first story. An old community complaint about missing JS offline persistence predates this documented capability and does not concretely contradict it. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that queued local writes sync automatically on reconnect (implied, not stated), conflict-resolution details, per-platform/web persistence specifics, and independent hands-on corroboration.
